chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The 'Innain (the deaf-mute) is given a waiting period of one year; then if his wife wishes, she may marry (another), and if she wishes, she may remain (married to him).

key_terms.العِنَّينُ: The deaf-mute (one who is both deaf and mute)
key_terms.يُتَرَبَّصُ: Is waited for / A waiting period is observed

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and marital status ruling for a deaf-mute person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the *iddah* (waiting period) for a wife whose husband is *Innain* (deaf and mute), establishing a one-year period of observation. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic approach to balancing marital stability with the practical realities of communication and care, allowing the wife autonomy to either continue the marriage or seek divorce after the year elapses.
